questions.question: Explain the difference in boiling temperature between butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
questions.answer: Both have hydrogen bonding, but butan-1-ol has a straight chain with a larger surface area and stronger London forces; 2-methylpropan-2-ol is branched and more spherical, so it has weaker London forces and a lower boiling temperature
steps: Both alcohols form hydrogen bonds between their -OH groups
Butan-1-ol has an unbranched chain, so molecules pack closely and have a larger surface area
Larger surface area gives stronger London forces between molecules
2-methylpropan-2-ol is branched and more spherical, so it has weaker London forces and boils at a lower temperature

questions.question: Complete the diagram to show the strongest intermolecular force between two molecules of butan-1-ol, including the intermolecular bond angle.

The O-H...O bond angle is 180 degrees (linear)

questions.question: Complete the equation for the complete combustion of butan-1-ol (state symbols not required).

4 carbon atoms give 4 CO2
10 hydrogen atoms give 5 H2O; oxygen balance: 1 + 12 = 8 + 5 = 13
So 6 O2 is needed

questions.question: A data book value for the molar enthalpy change of combustion of butan-1-ol is -2670 kJ mol-1. Give two reasons for the difference from the value calculated using mean bond enthalpies.
questions.answer: Mean bond enthalpies are averages, not exact for butan-1-ol; and the data book value uses liquid water (and butanol as liquid), whereas bond enthalpies assume gaseous species

Data book values use the actual physical states (liquid butanol, liquid water), while bond enthalpies assume gases
The energy needed to vaporise the liquid is therefore not included in the bond enthalpy calculation

questions.question: Biobutanol mixes with petrol in any proportion but bioethanol does not. Explain why petrol is more miscible with biobutanol than with bioethanol.
questions.answer: Biobutanol has a longer hydrocarbon chain, so it has similar London forces to the alkanes in petrol; bioethanol's short chain leaves its polar OH group dominant, so it mixes poorly
steps: Petrol is a mixture of non-polar alkanes held together by London forces
Butanol has a 4-carbon chain that is largely non-polar, so it interacts with alkanes by London forces
Ethanol has a short chain, so its polar -OH group dominates and hydrogen bonding with itself prevents mixing with alkanes
So biobutanol is more miscible with petrol

questions.question: Acidified hydrogen peroxide is added to iodide ions, and iodine and water are the only products. Write half-equations for the oxidation and reduction reactions (state symbols not required).
questions.answer: Oxidation: 2I- -> I2 + 2e-; Reduction: H2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> 2H2O
steps: Iodide is oxidised from -1 to 0, losing an electron each: 2I- -> I2 + 2e-
H2O2 is reduced from -1 to -2 in water, gaining 2 electrons
Balance with 2H+ and H2O: H2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> 2H2O

questions.question: Use the half-equations to write the overall equation for the redox reaction of iodide ions with acidified hydrogen peroxide.
steps: Add the two half-equations: 2I- -> I2 + 2e- and H2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> 2H2O
Electrons cancel
Overall: 2I- + H2O2 + 2H+ -> I2 + 2H2O

questions.topic: Colours of Iodine Solvent Extraction Layers
questions.question: State the colour of the aqueous layer and of the cyclohexane layer after solvent extraction of iodine.
questions.answer: Aqueous layer: pale or colourless (very little iodine left); cyclohexane layer: purple (violet)
steps: Most of the iodine dissolves in cyclohexane
Iodine in cyclohexane gives a purple (violet) solution
The aqueous layer is nearly colourless because little iodine remains in water

questions.topic: Solubility of Iodine in Cyclohexane and Water
questions.question: Explain why iodine is very soluble in cyclohexane but only slightly soluble in water.
questions.answer: Iodine and cyclohexane are both non-polar and interact by London forces; water is polar with hydrogen bonds that iodine cannot form with, so iodine is only slightly soluble
steps: Iodine is a non-polar molecule
Cyclohexane is non-polar, so iodine and cyclohexane interact by London forces (like dissolves like)
Water is polar and forms hydrogen bonds between its own molecules
Iodine cannot form strong attractions to water, so it is only slightly soluble

questions.question: Identify, by name or formula, a suitable drying agent for the cyclohexane layer.

steps: The drying agent must absorb water without reacting with cyclohexane or iodine
Anhydrous salts such as MgSO4 absorb water to form hydrated salts
Anhydrous magnesium sulfate is a suitable drying agent

questions.topic: Oxidation of Propan-1-ol to Propanoic Acid
questions.question: Write the balanced equation for the oxidation of propan-1-ol to propanoic acid, using [O] for oxygen from the oxidising agent (state symbols not required).
questions.answer: CH3CH2CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3CH2COOH + H2O
steps: Propan-1-ol is oxidised to the aldehyde (propanal) and then to the acid
Each oxidation step uses one [O]: primary alcohol to aldehyde (+[O], -H2O), then aldehyde to acid (+[O])
Overall: CH3CH2CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3CH2COOH + H2O

questions.question: Propan-1-ol is heated with concentrated acidified potassium dichromate(VI). Explain how the conditions affect the rate of reaction and ensure that propanoic acid is the only organic product.
questions.answer: Heat under reflux with excess concentrated oxidising agent: heating increases the rate, reflux returns the volatile propanal to be oxidised further to propanoic acid, so the acid is the only organic product
steps: Heating increases the rate of reaction (more particles have energy above Ea)
Propanal is volatile and would distil off before being oxidised if the mixture were just distilled
Heating under reflux returns the propanal to the flask, where it is oxidised to propanoic acid
Excess concentrated acidified dichromate(VI) ensures complete oxidation of the aldehyde to the acid
Propanoic acid is the only organic product, and the orange dichromate turns green

questions.question: Give a reason why using universal indicator to check for propanoic acid in the reaction mixture is not likely to be conclusive.
questions.answer: The reaction mixture is already acidic (acidified dichromate contains sulfuric acid), so universal indicator would show acidity whether or not propanoic acid is present
steps: The oxidising mixture contains acid (acidified potassium dichromate(VI))
Universal indicator responds to any acid present
So the colour does not show that propanoic acid specifically is present

questions.question: Phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator for the titration of propanoic acid with NaOH. State the colour change at the end-point.

The colour changes from colourless to a permanent pale pink

questions.question: Explain the type of bonding that occurs between the nitrogen atom and the hydrogen ion when the positive ion of DMAA forms.
questions.answer: A dative (coordinate) covalent bond: the lone pair on N is donated to the H+ ion, giving an N-H+ bond in which both electrons come from N
steps: The nitrogen atom in DMAA has a lone pair of electrons
The H+ ion accepts this lone pair, forming a new N-H bond
Both electrons in the new bond come from the nitrogen, so it is a dative (coordinate) covalent bond
The nitrogen becomes positively charged (an ammonium ion)

questions.question: Show how the ions formed when DMAA reacts with hydrochloric acid interact with water molecules, by completing diagrams.
questions.answer: The positive DMAA-H+ ion forms hydrogen bonds to water (delta- O of water to delta+ H on N); the Cl- ion is attracted to the delta+ H atoms of water

The delta+ H of water is attracted to the negative Cl- ion (ion-dipole)
Each ion is surrounded by water molecules, which dissolve it

questions.question: 2-methylpentan-3-ol reacts with concentrated phosphoric(V) acid. How many different alkenes can form? A one, B two, C three, D four.

steps: The OH is on C3; H can be lost from C2 or C4

Loss of H from C4 gives 4-methylpent-2-ene, which has E and Z isomers

questions.topic: Conditions for Ethanol from Ethene and Steam
questions.question: Explain the chemical reasons for the conditions used in the industrial hydration of ethene (300 C, 60 atm, phosphoric(V) acid catalyst) and why a low initial yield of 5% is acceptable.
questions.answer: Moderate temperature balances rate and yield (reaction exothermic); high pressure increases yield (2 gas moles to 1); catalyst gives a faster rate; low yield is acceptable because unreacted ethene and steam are recycled
steps: The reaction is exothermic (delta H = -45 kJ mol-1), so a low temperature gives a higher equilibrium yield
300 C gives a fast enough rate for a reasonable time while keeping equilibrium yield acceptable
60 atm favours the side with fewer gas moles (2 mol to 1 mol), increasing equilibrium yield
High pressure increases rate too, but higher pressure costs more to produce
The phosphoric(V) acid catalyst lowers the activation energy, so equilibrium is reached faster
A 5% yield is acceptable because unreacted ethene and steam are separated and recycled, so the overall yield is high and economical

questions.question: Explain why ethanol and water mix together fully.
questions.answer: Ethanol and water both have -OH groups that form hydrogen bonds with each other, so the new intermolecular attractions are as strong as those they replace
steps: Both ethanol and water have O-H groups
Hydrogen bonds form between ethanol's O-H and water's O (or H), with delta+ H and delta- O
The attractions between the two different molecules are similar in strength to those in the pure liquids
So the two liquids mix in any proportion

questions.question: Draw the structure of compound Y, the other organic product of oxidising ethanol with acidified dichromate(VI).

Structure: CH3-CHO, with C=O on the terminal carbon

questions.topic: Conditions for Ethanal and Ethanoic Acid

questions.answer: Ethanal: distil off the product as it forms (warm, with excess ethanol); ethanoic acid: heat under reflux with excess oxidising agent
steps: Ethanal is volatile, so it is distilled off as soon as it forms, preventing further oxidation
Ethanoic acid is maximised by heating under reflux with excess acidified dichromate(VI)
Reflux returns any volatile intermediate to be oxidised further

questions.question: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using bioethanol in petrol.
questions.answer: Advantage: renewable and carbon neutral (plants absorb CO2 as they grow); disadvantage: lower energy per dm3 than petrol, and it uses land and crops that could be food
steps: Bioethanol is made from plant material, which is renewable
Plants absorb CO2 as they grow, so the CO2 released is roughly balanced (carbon neutral)
Ethanol releases less energy per dm3 (23 MJ) than petrol (32 MJ)
Growing crops for fuel uses land that could grow food

questions.question: Suggest why the fermentation must be carried out in the absence of air.
questions.answer: Oxygen would oxidise the ethanol to ethanoic acid, and yeast enzymes only ferment ethanol under anaerobic conditions
steps: Fermentation is anaerobic: yeast converts glucose to ethanol and CO2 without oxygen
If air is present, oxygen oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid
This lowers the yield and purity of ethanol

questions.question: Suggest how the ethanol can be obtained from the fermentation mixture after filtering.
questions.answer: Fractional distillation (distil off the ethanol, which boils at a lower temperature than water)
steps: Ethanol has a lower boiling temperature (78 C) than water (100 C)
Heat the mixture and collect the vapour that condenses at about 78 C
Use fractional distillation to separate the ethanol from water

questions.question: Give a possible reason why ethanol is able to absorb water from the air.
questions.answer: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with water molecules through their O-H groups
steps: Ethanol has a polar O-H group
The O-H group forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules
So water is held in the liquid, making ethanol hygroscopic

questions.question: Suggest a problem arising from the hygroscopic nature of ethanol when using this fuel in a motor vehicle.
questions.answer: Absorbed water lowers the energy released by the fuel and can cause the ethanol and water to separate or corrode engine parts
steps: Ethanol absorbs water from the air over time
Water in the fuel lowers its energy content
Water can cause phase separation, corrosion of engine parts, or poor combustion

questions.question: Explain why the typical conditions of 300 C and 60 atm with phosphoric acid catalyst are used in the hydration of ethene, describing the effect of temperature and pressure on rate, equilibrium yield and cost.
questions.answer: 300 C gives a reasonable rate but is exothermic so yield falls with temperature; 60 atm increases yield and rate (fewer gas moles) but costs more; the catalyst increases rate without affecting yield, so the conditions are a compromise
steps: Higher temperature increases the rate of reaction
The forward reaction is exothermic, so higher temperature lowers the equilibrium yield
300 C is a compromise between a fast rate and an acceptable yield
Higher pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (2 mol gas to 1 mol), raising the yield, and also increases the rate
But higher pressure needs stronger, more expensive equipment and more energy, so 60 atm is a compromise
The phosphoric(V) acid catalyst increases the rate without changing equilibrium yield or adding cost in heating

questions.question: Label the axes of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve and use it to explain how the phosphoric acid catalyst increases the rate of hydration of ethene.
questions.answer: Axes: y-axis = number of molecules (fraction of molecules), x-axis = molecular energy; catalyst lowers Ea, so more molecules have energy >= Ea and the rate increases
steps: Label the y-axis as number (or fraction) of molecules and the x-axis as molecular energy (kinetic energy)
Mark the activation energy Ea on the x-axis for the uncatalysed and catalysed reactions
The catalyst moves Ea to the left, lowering the activation energy
More molecules now have energy >= Ea, so more successful collisions occur and the rate increases; the distribution itself is unchanged

questions.question: Suggest the advantage of using a support material containing lots of pores for the catalyst.
questions.answer: The pores give a large surface area for the catalyst, so more reactant molecules contact the catalyst and the rate increases
steps: A porous support has a very large surface area
More catalyst is exposed to the reactants
The rate of reaction increases

questions.question: Under these conditions only about 5% of the ethene is converted into ethanol per pass. Suggest how the overall yield of the process can be improved to make it economically viable.
questions.answer: Separate the ethanol from the mixture and recycle the unreacted ethene and steam back to the reactor
steps: Only 5% of ethene reacts per pass over the catalyst
Cool the gases and separate the ethanol from unreacted ethene and water
Recycle the unreacted ethene and steam back into the reactor so they can react again
The overall yield approaches a much higher value

questions.question: Compare and contrast the reactions of 2-bromopropane with potassium hydroxide in aqueous solution and in ethanolic solution. Include equations.
questions.answer: Aqueous KOH gives substitution to propan-2-ol (CH3CHBrCH3 + OH- -> CH3CH(OH)CH3 + Br-); ethanolic KOH gives elimination to propene (CH3CHBrCH3 + OH- -> CH2=CHCH3 + H2O + Br-)
steps: Aqueous KOH: OH- acts as a nucleophile and replaces Br, giving propan-2-ol: CH3CHBrCH3 + OH- -> CH3CH(OH)CH3 + Br-
Ethanolic KOH: OH- acts as a base and removes H+ from a carbon next to C-Br, giving propene: CH3CHBrCH3 + OH- -> CH2=CHCH3 + H2O + Br-
Substitution is favoured in water, where water solvates the ions and OH- is a good nucleophile
Elimination is favoured in ethanol, which is a poorer solvent for OH- and is less nucleophilic
Both reactions are initiated by OH- and both produce Br-; the conditions decide which product forms
Both products come from the same secondary halide, so the choice of solvent alone determines the product

questions.question: Explain why Step 2 (TiCl4 + 2Mg -> Ti + 2MgCl2) is a redox reaction, referring to relevant oxidation numbers.

questions.question: Titanium(IV) chloride reacts violently with water to produce white smoke used in naval smoke screens. Suggest the type of reaction and the compound producing the white smoke.
questions.answer: Hydrolysis; the white smoke is hydrogen chloride (HCl) fumes, together with titanium oxide particles
steps: TiCl4 reacts with water (H2O), which is a hydrolysis reaction
TiCl4 + 2H2O -> TiO2 + 4HCl
The HCl gas combines with water vapour in air to give white fumes (white smoke)

questions.question: Give the reason why excess steam is used in the first reaction, where methane reacts with steam to give hydrogen.
questions.answer: Excess steam shifts the equilibrium to the right to increase the yield of hydrogen (and helps prevent carbon forming on the catalyst)
steps: CH4 + H2O -> CO + 3H2 is reversible, with more gas moles on the right
Excess steam is a reactant, so it shifts the equilibrium to the right
This increases the yield of hydrogen and reduces carbon deposition

questions.question: Predict which of T1 and T2 is the higher temperature (T1 for methane with steam, T2 for CO with steam), and justify your answer.
questions.answer: T1 is higher: methane with steam is strongly endothermic and needs high temperature, whereas CO with steam is exothermic and is favoured at the lower temperature T2
steps: CH4 + H2O -> CO + 3H2 is endothermic, so high temperature favours it
CO + H2O -> CO2 + H2 is exothermic, so lower temperature favours the product
So T1 is the higher temperature

questions.question: Derive the overall equation for the production of H2 in Stage 1.

steps: Step 1: CH4 + H2O -> CO + 3H2
Step 2: CO + H2O -> CO2 + H2
Adding them, CO cancels: CH4 + 2H2O -> CO2 + 4H2

questions.question: Suggest one reason why CO2 is removed in the third reaction of Stage 1.
questions.answer: CO2 would poison the iron catalyst used in Stage 2 (and removing it purifies the hydrogen)
steps: CO2 is not wanted in the Stage 2 ammonia synthesis
Impurities such as CO2 poison (deactivate) the iron catalyst
Removing it leaves pure hydrogen for the reaction

questions.question: Name the type of reaction that occurs when CO2 is removed using aqueous N-methyldiethanolamine.

The amine reacts with CO2 in a reversible acid-base reaction
This removes CO2 from the gas stream

questions.answer: Advantage: higher pressure shifts equilibrium right (4 mol gas to 2 mol), increasing the ammonia yield; disadvantage: higher cost of equipment and energy for compression

Higher pressure needs stronger, more expensive equipment and more energy to compress the gases

questions.question: Give one reason why a high temperature is needed in the reaction of NH3 with O2 to form NO at 1100 K.
questions.answer: A high temperature gives particles enough energy to exceed the activation energy, so the reaction proceeds at a useful rate
steps: Higher temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles
More particles have energy >= Ea
So the rate of reaction is high enough for industrial use

questions.question: Suggest why only a small amount of energy is needed to maintain the temperature at 1100 K.
questions.answer: The oxidation of ammonia is strongly exothermic, so the reaction releases enough heat to maintain its own temperature
steps: Ammonia oxidation (4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O) is exothermic
The heat released keeps the reactor at the required temperature
So only a small amount of external energy is needed

questions.topic: Effect of Water on NO2 Yield
questions.question: Explain how adding water in the second reaction (where NO2 reacts with water to make HNO3) affects the yield of NO2 in the first reaction (2NO + O2 <=> 2NO2).
questions.answer: Water removes NO2 by converting it to HNO3, so the equilibrium 2NO + O2 <=> 2NO2 shifts to the right, increasing the yield of NO2
steps: NO2 is used up when it reacts with water to form nitric acid
Removing a product lowers its concentration
By Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium shifts to the right to replace the NO2 removed
So the yield of NO2 increases

questions.question: A sample of propane-1,2-diol (1.52 g) reacts completely with excess PCl5. What is the maximum mass of organic product in grams? Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0, Cl 35.5. A 1.13, B 1.89, C 2.26, D 4.52.
steps: Mr propane-1,2-diol C3H8O2 = 76.0; moles = 1.52 / 76.0 = 0.0200 mol

The answer is C

questions.question: Explain why alcohol B is completely soluble in ethanol but only slightly soluble in water.
questions.answer: B's OH group hydrogen-bonds with ethanol (which has a short chain and OH), so they mix; the large hydrocarbon part of B cannot be accommodated by water's hydrogen-bonded network, so B is only slightly soluble
steps: Alcohol B has an O-H group that forms hydrogen bonds with both ethanol and water
Ethanol has a short hydrocarbon chain, so it mixes fully with B by hydrogen bonds and London forces
Water forms a strong hydrogen-bonded network; the large non-polar hydrocarbon part of B disrupts it
So B dissolves only slightly in water, while it is fully soluble in ethanol

questions.question: What amount in mol of [O] is needed to convert 1 mol of pentane-1,3,5-triol into 3-oxopentanedioic acid and water? A 2, B 3, C 4, D 5.
questions.answer: D (5 mol)

questions.topic: Standard Enthalpy of Formation of Oxygen
questions.question: State why the standard enthalpy change of formation of oxygen is 0.0 kJ mol-1.
questions.answer: Oxygen is an element in its standard state (O2 gas), so no enthalpy change is needed to form it
steps: Standard enthalpy of formation is the enthalpy change to form 1 mol of a compound from its elements
Oxygen is an element in its most stable form under standard conditions (O2(g))
No formation reaction is needed, so the value is zero by definition

questions.question: The enthalpy change calculated from bond enthalpies in (a) is less accurate than the Hess cycle value. Give two reasons for this difference.
questions.answer: Bond enthalpies are mean values averaged over many compounds, not exact for methanol; and they assume all species are gases, ignoring phase changes
steps: Mean bond enthalpies are averages taken from different compounds, so they are approximate for each specific bond
Bond enthalpy calculations assume all reactants and products are in the gas state
Standard enthalpies of formation use the actual physical states of the substances

questions.question: Suggest two possible advantages, other than increasing the yield, of a one-step synthesis of methanol using a catalyst instead of the two-step process.
questions.answer: Fewer reaction steps and less equipment (lower capital cost); lower pressure and energy needs, so less recycling of unreacted gases is required
steps: A one-step process needs less equipment and fewer reactors
It needs less energy and smaller pressure requirements than the two-step process
Less recycling and separation of unreacted gases is needed, which saves cost and time

questions.question: Many catalysts have been used for one-step methanol synthesis (including metal oxides). State two characteristics that all these catalysts have.
questions.answer: They are solids (heterogeneous catalysts) that provide a surface; they are not used up in the reaction and lower the activation energy
steps: All these catalysts are solids with a large surface area where reactants adsorb
They provide an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
They are unchanged at the end of the reaction and can be reused

questions.question: A one-step methanol process is carried out at 101 kPa and 800 C. Deduce how the reaction conditions could be changed to increase the yield, explaining why such changes may not be economical.
questions.answer: Increase the pressure (fewer gas moles on the product side) and lower the temperature (the reaction is exothermic); both raise yield but cost more for high-pressure equipment and energy, and lower temperature slows the rate
steps: The synthesis of methanol from CO and H2 has fewer gas moles on the product side (e.g. CO + 2H2 -> CH3OH: 3 mol gas to 1 mol)
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right, increasing the yield
The forward reaction is exothermic, so lowering the temperature also increases the yield
High pressures need expensive, strong equipment and more energy to compress gases
Lower temperature slows the rate, so a catalyst or longer time would be needed, which is also costly
